finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL with http.Get. The only check is a substring match for "example.io", so any URL containing that text is accepted, including internal ones. The response body is returned to the caller.
finding.source: main.go:31 - r.FormValue("logo"), attacker-controlled via query string or POST form
finding.sink: main.go:36 - http.Get(raw) using http.DefaultClient; full response body copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: raw is the attacker-controlled 'logo' form/query value
Guard: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is a substring check, not a hostname check, so the text can sit in a query, fragment, path, or userinfo
http.Get(raw) requests whatever host the URL names
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the internal response to the attacker (non-blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: Only line 32, which is bypassed by e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io or http://127.0.0.1:<port>/x?example.io. No scheme allowlist (non-http schemes fail and the nil resp then panics at line 37, a crash not SSRF). No hostname or IP check blocking private, loopback, or link-local addresses. No redirect restriction: default client follows up to 10 redirects, so an open redirect on an allowed host would bypass even a correct host check. No timeout.

verdict.guard_found: Only main.go:32, strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"). This is a substring check, not an exact hostname or anchored match, so it does not close the finding. No scheme, host, or IP restriction exists before the sink at main.go:36, and nothing else in the path validates the URL.
verdict.reason: The source is r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31, which any remote client can set via query string or form body. The only check, the substring test at main.go:32, can be satisfied by putting "example.io" in a query or path while the host is internal, and http.Get(raw) at main.go:36 then fetches it and io.Copy at main.go:38 returns the body to the attacker. All trace lines match the code.
